articles.title: Fantasy Football: Here are Joel Smyth's top-50 stats you need to know before the 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: Be sure to bookmark these important stats going into the 2026 fantasy football season.
articles.body:
What is fantasy football but tracking stats? Statistics are so important when playing fantasy for really any sport. When we consider fantasy football, stats can help separate the good picks from the great picks in your draft. After a full offseason of research, fantasy football analyst Joel Smyth gives his top-50 fantasy stats to know before the biggest draft weekend of the year!

50. Since 2019, the difference in PPG from a top-eight pick to Picks 9-12 in the first round is only 0.5 in PPR (if your guy is going ninth on average and you have Pick 5, just go get your guy).

49. The only starting QB since 2024 with zero carries from inside the two yard line is Lamar Jackson.

48. After leading the NFL in deep targets with 32, DK Metcalf dropped down to 17 in 2025 with Aaron Rodgers despite a heavily vertical route tree.

47. In his third straight season with his fantasy PPG decreasing, Travis Kelce ranked 28th among TE in red-zone target share.

46. Minnesota and its WRs were bad last year. Yet still, Kevin O'Connell's offenses rank fifth in receiving PPG in his four seasons with the Vikings.

45. In Travis Hunter's four games with 20+ defensive snaps, he averaged 5.8 PPG (13.5 PPG and 2x more targets in other three games).

44. Puka Nacua's targets per route since 2024 is 36.8%. No other qualified player is over 30%.

43. Dalton Kincaid ranked first among tight ends in targets/route, yards/route, yds/target, yds/reception, 1st downs/route, targeted passer rating, yds/target over expected, fantasy pts/route and expected fantasy pts/route in 2025. Efficiency is not the problem; he just needs more routes (<25% of run-blocking snaps).

42. Denver's offense (14th in scoring) ranked seventh in WR fantasy points, despite a much weaker WR room compared to other top-10 teams. (AKA, Waddle bump)

41. The top three QBs in checkdown percentage were all Cincinnati QBs in 2025 (yay, Chase Brown!).

40. Since entering the NFL, Christian McCaffrey has four of the five best PPR seasons in fantasy football (Barkley 2018). Unparalleled ceiling.

39. Dolphins QB Malik Willis is fifth in fantasy points/snap among QBs since 2023 and first in 2025.

38. In Jacksonville's final four games, Parker Washington had 454 receiving yards. Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers combined for 267, despite both having more routes than Washington.

37. Cardinals TE Trey McBride had 667 routes in 2025. Ja'Marr Chase was second with 613, Travis Kelce second among TE with 511.

36. Colts TE Tyler Warren's target/route skyrocketed from 21% with Michael Pittman Jr. on the field to 30% without. For comparison, McBride's target/route in 2025 was 24.4%.

35. CMC was the only RB above 2.0 combined goal line carries + red zone targets. But in 2024, both Kareem Hunt and Chuba Hubbard were above 2.0 as well (great for Kenneth Walker III and Hubbard's potential).

34. The highest catch rate on deep balls in 2025:

1. Kayshon Boutte 2. Stefon Diggs 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba 4. Puka Nacua

Drake Maye WRs were the top-two and now A.J. Brown is in town in New England.

33. Rome Odunze had 55% of his end zone targets deemed "inaccurate." The next closest was 37%. DJ Moore also vacated 13 end-zone targets, fourth most among WRs.

32. Luther Burden III ranked eighth in fantasy points per snap as a rookie. Six of the seven WRs above him were fantasy WR1s.

31. Travis Etienne Jr. was 35th in explosive carry %, but 14th in explosive yards (biggest diff in RB). His explosive points far outweighed his per attempt production. He also was the only RB with multiple explosive receiving TDs (3, 1 prior in career).

30. Ravens WR Zay Flowers 4.83 yds/route on play action was the second-best among WR. Play action %: Baltimore 26th, Chicago (Baltimore's new OC, Declan Doyle, came from the Bears) second.

29. In his last 17 games with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase has exactly 200 targets (Amon-Ra St. Brown was second to Chase in targets in 2025 with 172 in 17 games).

28. In total RB volume (expected fantasy points), SF, DET, & ATL were unsurprisingly top-three. Fourth was the Steelers, with multiple RBs in the top 24 in volume.

27. Tetairoa McMillan had 16 targets dropped/or a WR error in his rookie season (T-most in NFL w/ BTJ. I'd expect this to bounce back in a major way in Year 2).

26. Justin Jefferson has failed to hit his season average in fantasy points in all six fantasy championships (10.6 PPG).

25. Kyler Murray only played five games in 2025, but he was the fantasy QB5 (PPG) from 2019-2024 and a QB1 in all six seasons. Kevin O'Connell's QBs have finished QB12, QB6, QB9, QB30 in Minnesota.

24. Kyle Pitts Sr. was the TE5 last season, but the distance in PPG to the TE4 is the same as the distance to TE15.

23. Jaguars HC Liam Coen's QB ranks third in fantasy PPG since 2024 (players ahead were Allen, Jackson) and fourth in passing PPG (behind only Burrow, Goff, Stafford).

22. Jalen Hurts will have his fifth play-caller in five years in 2026. All four previous play-callers have given the Eagles QB over 40% of the team's goal-line carries. (Nick Sirianni's gonna tush push).

21. Trevor Lawrence and Jared Goff, former No. 1 overall picks, went from bottom-four QBs as rookies to QB11 in Year 2. Cam Ward finished as the QB32 in 2025 with the league's hardest fantasy QB schedule.

20. In the last 10 years, only two of 33 RBs in the first four rounds to score 20+ PPG came in Rounds 3-4, while seven of 30 WRs to score 20+ PPG did.

19. DeVonta Smith, Luther Burden III and Ladd McConkey, all players who played a lot in the slot in 2025, were all much better in yards per route outside, contrary to popular belief on some. All three should play more outside in new offenses/WR rooms in 2026 (increases in yds/route: Smith +150%, Burden +59%, McConkey +39%).

18. Davante Adams' 7.9 PPG on end-zone targets in 2025 was the most since 2007 Randy Moss. In 2008, Moss dipped down to 3.1.

17. Of top-12 drafted RBs in the NFL Draft in recent history, only Christian McCaffrey and Bijan Robinson did not score 15+ PPG as rookies before Jeanty failed to as well. In Year 2, Bijan was RB3 overall; CMC RB2 overall.

16. Lamar Jackson had five TDs dropped in 2025, the most in the NFL, even though he was last in pass att/gm and only played 13 games (also does not count the Isaiah Likely end-zone fumble).

15. Emeka Egbuka was the only WR to play a top-five fantasy WR defense five times, without playing a single bottom-five WR defense (Tampa Bay had the hardest WR schedule of 2025).

14. Jahmyr Gibbs was second in yds/att in gap schemes, and 42nd in zone schemes last season. James Conner led the NFL in gap schemes (69%) in 2024 w/ Drew Petzing as OC.

13. Jadarian Price had a PFF pass blocking grade of 38.5 in his college career (bad). The bottom-three RBs in pass blocking grade from 2025 were rookies.

12. Kansas City and Andy Reid ranked fifth in RB PPG from 2014-2023 (29th in the last two seasons).

11. When taking just Chase Brown's starts in 2024, Zac Taylor has produced a fantasy RB1 in each of his last six seasons as Cincinnati's head coach.

10. De'Von Achane averages 11.4 receiving PPG w/ Tua Tagovailoa in his career. In his eight games without, that drops to 3.4.

9. Josh McDaniels has been OC/HC for 19 years. His RB1 has hit 60% of the team RB touches only 5 times, with only 3 RBs crossing 15+ PPR PPG (2022 Raiders Josh Jacobs, 2012 Rams Stephen Jackson, 2010 Broncos Knowshon Moreno).

8. Jaylen Warren was top-two among RB in targets/route, yards/route and missed tackles/reception in 2025. PIT has the most vacated RB targets with 82.

7. Thirty-five "passing" QBs have been drafted in Rounds 2-5 since 2015, with a hit rate of 31% ... rushing QBs are at 63%, while Josh Allen is at 100%.

6. Josh Allen has finished top-two in fantasy points among QBs in each of the last six seasons. Nobody else has finished top-two twice.

5. Ladd McConkey's yards per route increase by 96% with motion. Mike McDaniel runs the most motion in the NFL.

4. In my luck metric stat, CeeDee Lamb was the unluckiest player of 2025, with -2.7 PPG from his "bad luck."

3. Drake Maye was the QB32 in the fourth quarter last season, and QB1 from quarters 1-3. The Patriots' schedule now makes them the favorite in only 10 games.

2. Here are the cornerbacks Brian Thomas Jr. is set to face in the first eight weeks of the season: Denzel Ward, Patrick Surtain II, Christian Gonzalez, DJ Turner, Quinyon Mitchell, Derek Stingley Jr., BYE, Sauce Gardner.

1. Fourteen RBs have been selected top-25 in the NFL Draft since 2015. Of the first 11 RBs in the group, ALL 11 had an RB1 fantasy season by their second year. Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton can make it 13 for 13 in their sophomore year with an RB1 season (plus, Jeremiyah Love).

articles.title: Michael Strahan reportedly welcomes baby No. 5 with younger girlfriend after Isabella’s cancer battle
articles.summary: NFL News: Michael Strahan just became a dad again. Quietly. Like, really quietly. The 54-year-old \"Good Morning America\" anchor and former NFL star and his long.
articles.body: Michael Strahan just became a dad again. Quietly. Like, really quietly. The 54-year-old "Good Morning America" anchor and former NFL star and his longtime girlfriend, Kayla Quick, welcomed a baby girl earlier this year. Nobody said a word. Not Strahan, not Quick, not GMA. TMZ says it learned this from unnamed sources "with direct knowledge," so this is not confirmed by Strahan himself. No baby name, no birth date, nothing official yet. Just a report.Michael Strahan’s secret baby bombshell just opened up a whole new mystery about his longtime girlfriendHere's why this is actually wild: Strahan and Quick have been together since 2015. Ten years. And in that whole decade, they've barely been photographed together. A few red carpets, one Christmas card cameo, a football game here and there, a Duke campus visit to see his daughter.That's basically the entire public record of this relationship. Compare that to how loud Strahan gets about everything else in his family. He went on Jimmy Fallon to gush about becoming a grandpa in 2024, he posted through daughter Isabella's brain cancer battle in real time, on-air, for years. This man does not usually do quiet.Except with Kayla, apparently. She's kept an even lower profile than he has.Who is Kayla Quick? Michael Strahan’s girlfriend has a little-known history now back in focusQuick, 33, runs a wellness supplement brand called FIZZNESS and studied at the University of Tampa before pursuing culinary and nutrition programs in New York.Quick has a criminal history from her teens. At 14, she was reportedly cited for disorderly conduct in her hometown of Port Charlotte, Florida. Then in May 2005, at 18, she was arrested for grand theft after she and her then-boyfriend allegedly broke into her grandmother's home and took roughly $6,000 in jewelry, according to a Charlotte County Sheriff's arrest report. The charges were reportedly dropped, though the reasons why were never made public, meaning the case never resulted in a conviction.This would be baby No. 5 for Strahan and his first with Quick. His other four: Tanita (34) and Michael Jr. (31), from his first marriage to Wanda Hutchins (1992-1996), a marriage that started when they were teenagers in Germany, where Strahan's father was stationed. And twins Isabella and Sophia (21), from his second marriage to Jean Muggli (1999-2006), a relationship that ended in dueling abuse allegations, both denied and disputed, and one of the most expensive divorce settlements in sports history at the time.There's also this wrinkle that there were split rumors swirling around Strahan and Quick recently. So either they quietly had a baby and then quietly broke up, or the "split" chatter was overblown, or there's a timeline here nobody's actually cracked yet. TMZ's report doesn't clear any of that up, and until Strahan or Quick speaks, it's genuinely unclear which version is true.So treat this as a report, not a confirmed fact, until Strahan says something himself. But if it holds up, the man just added a fifth kid to a family he's spent a decade actively shielding from the spotlight, and somehow pulled it off without a single leak, tabloid photo, or slip-up until now.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Robert Saleh Calls Out 'Cheap' Hit By Bears' Woods on Wan'Dale Robinson After Titans WR's Injury
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh wasn't a fan of Chicago Bears safety Xavier Woods' hit on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson that resulted in an injury during a joint practice between the two teams on Thursday.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh wasn't a fan of Chicago Bears safety Xavier Woods' hit on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson that resulted in an injury during a joint practice between the two teams on Thursday.

"It was cheap," Saleh said, per ESPN's Turron Davenport .

Near the end of practice, Robinson caught a pass from Cam Ward across the middle of the field before he was hit by Woods.

The collision led to a scuffle involving players from both teams.

While Robinson was able to get up and walk off the field under his own power, Saleh confirmed that he was being evaluated for a concussion.

Titans left guard Peter Skoronski also called out the hit by Woods after practice.

"That's Teach Tape 101 in terms of what not to do in a thud practice and a thud period," Skoronski said, per Davenport. "You can't have guys like Wan'Dale going down like that, and hits like that aren't necessary. I get we're being competitive. I get DBs are physical and stuff like that, but that's totally uncalled for in a practice thing like this. We defend our teammates, man. I don't encourage throwing punches or fighting or anything like that, but if cheap shots are taken on our guys, it's unacceptable for us."

Robinson is expected to operate as a key piece of Tennessee's passing attack this season after signing a four-year, $78 million contract with the team in free agency.

During his 2025 campaign with the New York Giants, he hauled in 92 receptions for a career-high 1,014 yards while finding the end zone four times.

As for Woods, he joined the Bears on Aug. 7 after recording 39 tackles and three passes defended across 11 games as a member of the Titans last season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce scored another major business win as his 400% growth fuels a powerful Hollywood expansion
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce has been building a life beyond the NFL, and his latest business move showed just how far that reach had grown. In October 2025, the Kans.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has been building a life beyond the NFL, and his latest business move showed just how far that reach had grown. In October 2025, the Kansas City Chiefs star’s connection to Garage Beer took an unexpected turn toward Hollywood. A new Predator-themed project featuring his brother Jason Kelce helped put the fast-growing beer brand in the spotlight while adding another layer to Travis’ expanding entertainment and business portfolio.Travis Kelce’s Garage Beer partnership gets a Hollywood boostThis story was first reported on October 31, 2025, making it last year’s news rather than a current development. At the time, Garage Beer was enjoying a major surge after Travis and Jason Kelce became investors and public faces of the brand in 2024.The attention grew even more when Jason appeared alongside former Philadelphia Eagles lineman Beau Allen in “Thermal Buzz,” a short promotional film connected to the Predator: Badlands universe. The project leaned into the brothers’ familiar humor and sports personalities while giving Garage Beer an unusual pop-culture platform.The opening line from Jason immediately set the tone: “Garage Beer saved my life.”The reference to classic 1980s action movies was more than a joke. It gave the campaign a personality that felt closely aligned with the Kelce brothers, who have built much of their public appeal around their relaxed, humorous approach.And the timing was significant for Garage Beer. According to the report, the company had seen its volume climb by more than 400% since the Kelces took stakes. Durational Capital’s investment also reportedly pushed the company’s valuation to about $200 million, while projected annual revenue had risen to between $60 million and $70 million.For Travis, the partnership highlighted a bigger trend. He was no longer simply attaching his name to brands. He was becoming part of the business story itself.Travis Kelce’s business empire stretches beyond footballThe Garage Beer investment fits neatly into the broader business strategy Travis has developed alongside his NFL career.His biggest media success has been New Heights, the podcast he hosts with Jason. What started as a sibling conversation has grown into a major entertainment platform, attracting high-profile guests and reaching audiences far beyond football. The brothers later signed a reported three-year deal with Amazon’s Wondery worth more than $100 million, further establishing their influence in sports media.Travis has also moved into traditional business ventures. He co-owns 1587 Prime, a Kansas City steakhouse with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and has held equity connected to Six Flags.What makes his approach particularly interesting is the variety. Football remains the foundation of Travis Kelce’s fame, but his investments increasingly connect sports, entertainment, food, media and consumer brands.The Hollywood crossover involving Garage Beer was therefore more than a promotional stunt. It reflected how the Kelce name had become a business asset capable of moving between different worlds.For an athlete still competing at the highest level, that is a striking position to reach. Travis Kelce was building the next chapter of his career while his NFL story was still being written.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Packers running back Josh Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges of battery, criminal damage to property
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested May 26 after police were called to his home to investigate a disturbance. He was released from jail the next day.
articles.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is facing misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from what police described as a physical confrontation with his girlfriend. Jacobs was arrested May 26 after police were called to his home to investigate a disturbance and was released from jail the next day. The charges were announced Thursday by Brown County District Attorney David Lasee. “Our office sought to ensure a fair and complete review of available evidence, some of which only recently became available to our office due to significant, ongoing forensic efforts by law enforcement,” Lasee said in a statement. “A criminal complaint is nothing more than a written, formal accusation against a defendant alleging the commission of criminal offenses and does not raise any inference of guilt. Mr. Jacobs is presumed innocent of these charges. “As this is an ongoing criminal case, and out of respect for the rights of all parties, our office will not have further comment on the matter at this time.” Jacobs’ lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III — issued a statement acknowledging the charges, noting they “do not include domestic violence.” “The allegations will be addressed in court, and not in the media,” they said. “Mr. Jacobs respects the District Attorney’s office and the process it followed.” Jacobs was back on the field with the Packers for organized team activities less than a week after the arrest and has been with the team for training camp, though he’s been limited by a groin injury. Jacobs was initially arrested on five criminal charges, including a felony count of strangulation and suffocation as well as battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct and intimidation of a victim. The only charges filed Thursday involved the misdemeanor counts of battery and disorderly conduct. Incident started with dispute over phone According to the criminal complaint, the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department responded to a report of a disturbance involving a man and a woman on the morning of May 23. Police said Jacobs’ girlfriend told them she had a lump on her head as a result of Jacobs’ actions. Police said the woman said she had been looking through Jacobs’ phone and saw he was talking to other women and that she threw the phone in anger without breaking it. She told police that Jacobs had her phone and that she told him he could look through it. Police said the woman indicated she tried to retrieve her phone from Jacobs, but he didn’t return it and instead grabbed her arm and began a struggle that lasted several minutes. Police said the two of them then left in separate vehicles, with the woman following Jacobs to try to get her phone back. They eventually returned to the home, and the woman said she was going to call police to get her phone back. Police said Jacobs called the woman a derogatory name and said he would “do something to her” as she grabbed a second phone from a duffel bag. According to police, the woman was trying to exit a garage door to get outside when Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took the phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. According to police, the woman said Jacobs hadn’t returned her primary phone, and that her second phone was damaged as a result of the incident. According to the criminal complaint, surveillance footage from the camera system in the garage corroborated the woman’s statement. The maximum possible sentence for each of the two charges filed against Jacobs includes nine months in jail and a $10,000 fine. A Packers spokesman didn’t immediately respond to a message seeking comment Thursday. The NFL said it is monitoring the case. Loss of Jacobs would challenge Packers Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season. That followed a 2024 season in which Jacobs ran for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns while earning his third Pro Bowl selection. The 28-year-old has rushed for 7,803 yards and 74 touchdowns in his seven-year career, which included five seasons with the Raiders. He earned All-Pro honors and had an NFL-leading 1,653 yards rushing with Las Vegas in 2022. Running back is a position in which the Packers don’t have much depth. Injuries have caused 2024 third-round draft pick MarShawn Lloyd to play just one game over the past two seasons, though he has been healthy throughout training camp. Pierre Strong Jr. spent last season on Green Bay’s practice squad but has 499 career yards rushing with the New England Patriots (2022) and Cleveland Browns (2023-24). Chris Brooks ran for 106 yards on 27 carries last season while contributing primarily on special teams. During a news conference Wednesday, Green Bay general manager Brian Gutekunst was asked if the Packers would need to add another running back in the event Jacobs faced charges and got suspended. “Yeah, I’m pretty confident we can sustain it, but it doesn’t mean we wouldn’t do that,” Gutekunst said about adding a player. “We’ll deal with that when that comes, but we’ve obviously prepared for that in case that happens. But at the same time, I feel really good about the guys we’ve got in that room, and I think we can survive that.”

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $325 million Kansas City Current investment has a deeper meaning as he opens up about his daughter and women’s sports
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has already changed the sporting landscape in Kansas City through his success with the Chiefs. But his ambitions have never stopped at.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has already changed the sporting landscape in Kansas City through his success with the Chiefs. But his ambitions have never stopped at football. In 2024, Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes stepped into women’s soccer ownership with the Kansas City Current, a move that reflected both their belief in the city and their desire to help create bigger opportunities for women athletes.Patrick Mahomes explains his Kansas City Current ownership decisionThis story was originally reported in March 2024, so it reflects Mahomes’ views at that time rather than a new 2026 development. The timing was significant because the Kansas City Current were preparing for their first game at CPKC Stadium, the first stadium in the world built specifically for an NWSL team.Ahead of that historic opening, Mahomes appeared on ESPN’s SportsCenter with Brittany and spoke about the excitement surrounding the new club. The atmosphere reminded him of the energy he regularly experienced at Arrowhead Stadium.“It’s been remarkable to be in the stadium and see the fans. I feel like I’m at Arrowhead, that’s the type of vibe I’m getting here. It’s going to be a historic day and the start of something great,” he said.But the decision to become part of the Current was about more than adding another investment to his growing portfolio. Mahomes connected the project to something much more personal.“Yeah, I just want to give back in the best way possible and to be making history in women’s sports, I have my own daughter, to give them the platform that they deserve. I mean, I’ve seen the type of talent they showcase every single game and we wanted to build a stadium that matched that talent. And to have it here in Kansas City as the first women’s-specific stadium, and it’s just the start of something that will kinda take off throughout the rest of the world.”That explanation offered a glimpse into what the ownership role meant to Mahomes. He was not simply buying into another professional sports franchise. He saw the Current as part of a larger opportunity to raise the profile of women’s soccer and give elite players a venue that matched their ability.Patrick Mahomes’ growing Kansas City sports ownership portfolioThe Current also became another piece of Mahomes’ remarkable connection with Kansas City sports.By 2024, the Chiefs quarterback had ownership interests in three major professional teams in the city. Along with the Current, he had invested in Sporting Kansas City and the Kansas City Royals. That put him in a rare position among active athletes, allowing him to contribute to several sports while continuing to build his own legacy on the football field.Mahomes also explained why Kansas City itself made those investments appealing.“For me, it just shows how much support Kansas City has. You go to any game, you see the fanbase and how much support,” explained Mahomes. “They really love the players for what they do on the field, but also off of it as well. It’s a great city. It’s the place me and Brittany want to raise our kids in, and it speaks to the people in this city.”That final point may be the heart of his ownership strategy. Mahomes has become one of Kansas City’s biggest sporting stars, but his investment choices suggest he wants his influence to extend beyond touchdowns and championships.His involvement with the Kansas City Current showed that legacy can take another form: helping build something that gives a new generation of athletes a bigger stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Rumors on Falcons QB1 Battle with Tua Losing 'Big-Time Lead' over Michael Penix Jr.
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa has lost an edge over Michael Penix Jr. in the battle for the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Tua Tagovailoa has lost an edge over Michael Penix Jr. in the battle for the Atlanta Falcons' starting quarterback job, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

"Tua Tagovailoa had a big-time lead in this race," Rapoport reported during a Thursday appearance on NFL GameDay (0:15 mark). "Really was his for the taking. That was the hope of the organization. That he would come in, play well, take the starting job and kind of move forward that way. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr. could just rehab, recover from that torn ACL, get back whenever healthy, then they would reassess at some point in the season if a change needed to be made."

"Tua has been inconsistent in practice, was inconsistent in the game," he added. "Seems like he has been practicing better the last couple of days, but the door is open for Michael Penix."

Tagovailoa signed a one-year contract with the Falcons in March after serving as the Miami Dolphins' starter from 2020-25.

He received plenty of opportunities to work with Atlanta's first-team offense, as Penix was sidelined throughout the beginning of training camp while he recovered from a torn ACL that he suffered after starting nine games for the Falcons last year.

Penix wasn't fully cleared to practice until Saturday.

Still, Tagovailoa wasn't able to gain separation atop Atlanta's depth chart.

During the Falcons' preseason opener, he mishandled a snap on his first drive and only finished 3-of-5 for 22 yards through two possessions. He's also experienced his fair share of struggles during joint practices.

Tagovailoa will have another opportunity to make his case for the Falcons' starter under center in their preseason finale, as he's set to open the contest.

Penix won't make an appearance despite being cleared.

Atlanta will face the Miami Dolphins on Friday at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Prosecutor says he has portion of Josh Jacobs' domestic incident with ex-girlfriend on video
articles.summary: Surveillance video from Josh Jacobs' garage allegedly corroborates his ex-girlfriend's account of the battery, raising questions about his NFL future.
articles.body: The District Attorney who charged Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs with two domestic misdemeanors on Thursday initially released a statement about reviewing new available evidence, and now we know that evidence is surveillance video related to the alleged battery. After police investigated the incident at the scene of Jacobs' alleged battery on his ex-girlfriend, they later did more legwork according to District Attorney David L. Lasee. And they uncovered a security camera in Jacobs' garage where he and his ex-girlfriend allegedly had a physical altercation. JOSH JACOBS FACES TWO MISDEMEANOR CHARGES AFTER MAY ARREST The incident report from Lasee's office says ANM, as they are identifying the player's ex-girlfriend, told officers as she was trying to exit the garage door to get outside, "Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground and she struck her head, suffering an injury," the report reads. "Jacobs then took her phone from her while she was on the ground. ANM laid on the ground for a while and then struggled to walk back into the house." ATTORNEY FOR DENVER BRONCOS DEFENDER JONATHON COOPER PLAYS RACE CARD IN DOMESTIC ABUSE CASE Lasee's incident report says this is on video. The "surveillance footage from the camera system within the garage of the Tretni Mar residence from May 23, 2026, between 8:30 a.m. and 8:38 a.m. corroborates the relevant portions of ANM's statement that one would expect to have seen on video, including both ANM and Jacobs departing the residence in their respective vehicles and returning to the residence, as well as their actions on the security camera in the garage. "The surveillance video further shows Jacobs took ANM's phone while she was on the floor of the garage, and approximately 40 seconds later, Jacobs returns to the garage and appears to damage ANM's phone." The video is not available for independent inspection at this time. It will obviously be used as evidence in the case against Jacobs. BRONCOS STAR SPEAKS OUT FOLLOWING DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST, FIRES OFF AN APOLOGY He was charged Thursday with one count of misdemeanor battery and one count of criminal damage to property. Jacobs turned himself in to police on May 26, three days after the incident at his Hobart, Wisconsin home. So far, the case has been tried in the court of public opinion as a he-said versus she-said account, with Jacobs enlisting a legal team that claims he will be exonerated of the allegations. But if the District Attorney's office indeed has a video that prosecutors say shows Jacobs getting physical with his ex-girlfriend in that garage, his legal situation will be much worse and his status as an NFL player could be at risk. The NFL, which studies practices, meetings, and games on tape, obviously frowns upon video of a battery by one of its employees and has a history of separating from such episodes. Ray Rice's career ended when a 2014 video of him striking his then-fiancée, Janay Palmer, in the face during an argument became public. The video Lasee viewed before deciding to charge Jacobs comes with its own backstory outlined in the DA's incident report: "Your complainant reviewed a follow up report from Investigator Van Lanen of the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department received on August 6, 2026, and a digital forensic examination report prepared by Frank Angel for the Brown County Sheriff’s Office, received on August 13, 2026. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "Those reports relate an on or about July 27 and 28, 2026, of recovered electronic devices from Jacobs’s residence, including components of a video surveillance system, as well as cellular phones from both Jacobs and ANM. "Angel’s report outlines the process used to conduct the forensic exam of the devices, and explained that the recovery of video files from the surveillance system was complex and took several weeks, culminating in a final verification on July 21, 2026. "Based on the foregoing, the complainant believes this complaint to be true and correct." The Packers released a statement about Thursday's charges. "We are aware of the charges brought against Josh Jacobs," the team said in a statement. "We will continue to cooperate with the NFL as we work through the process. We will have no further comment at this time." The NFL's investigation of the entire episode is ongoing and Jacobs is subject to discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy and may even be placed on the commissioner's exempt list, which would mean he'd get paid but cannot play. articles.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton buries Geoff Schwartz after analyst butchers Bo Nix's downfield game

articles.title: Tony Romo receives 3 new citations following OWI arrest in Milwaukee
articles.summary: Romo is due in court on Sept. 21. It's unclear if he'll call games for CBS Sports again.
articles.body:
Tony Romo has received three new citations stemming from his arrest in Milwaukee on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, according to the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel .

According to online court records, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS Sports analyst was cited for first-offense operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing on the right side and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle. Romo had already received a citation on July 27 for refusing to take an intoxication test after his arrest.

Romo is reportedly due in court for all four citations on Sept. 21.

His camp also released a new statement to the Journal-Sentinel:

"Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."

Romo was arrested on July 23 after being pulled over on a Milwaukee highway and performing poorly on a field sobriety test, according to police.

Romo was once the darling of NFL media and CBS paid him like it with a record-shattering 10-year, $180 million contract in 2020. His luster had worn off considerably even before the arrest, with his meandering and casual commentary style wearing thin for many fans .

So it might not be a surprise if CBS uses the arrest to get out of that contract and cut Romo loose. The Athletic noted his contract contains a morals clause that could allow CBS to void the deal if he embarrasses the company.

In the meantime, CBS is set to open the season with J.J. Watt working opposite Jim Nantz in its No. 1 booth.

articles.title: Dillon Gabriel, an afterthought in Browns' QB competition, has a fantastic preseason finale
articles.summary: Dillon Gabriel had a very efficient night against the Patriots.
articles.body:
Dillon Gabriel never really made a move in the Cleveland Browns' quarterback competition this preseason. Maybe he was never given a true shot.

Deshaun Watson was the QB1 most of the offseason, and when the Browns picked him as the starter it seemed like a predetermined outcome. Shedeur Sanders was the one who was said to have been competing with Watson. He got a start in the Browns' second preseason game ahead of Watson.

Gabriel, a third-round pick last year, never seemed like a consideration. That made Thursday night's performance a bit interesting.

Gabriel had a big first half for the Browns in the preseason finale against the New England Patriots as Watson and Sanders sat out. Gabriel was 12 of 15 for 186 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in the first half. His 157.9 passer rating was just short of a perfect mark, which is 158.3. The Browns scored on all five of Dillon's possessions in the first half, not counting a one-play drive before the half expired.

Watson was an unpopular pick as the Browns' starter for Week 1. Sanders didn't do enough to clearly win the job. There will be some wondering if Gabriel should have gotten a longer look, especially since Thursday night's game happened on a national Amazon Prime Video broadcast.

"What a great half, happy for him," Browns coach Todd Monken said during an Amazon Prime Video interview at halftime. "Guys played well around him. Certainly took advantage of his opportunity."

Thursday night's performance highlighted what Gabriel does well. He understands where to go with the ball, makes quick decisions and can accurately deliver short passes to playmakers. He doesn't have a cannon arm and won't often push the ball downfield, but he did roll out for one intermediate completion that turned into a 52-yard gain.

All of Gabriel's touchdowns were similar. They were quick passes that found the open spot in the defense and allowed the target to get into the end zone.

The Browns have made their decision with Watson and aren't going to turn back from it. But Cleveland is also likely to have multiple starting quarterbacks this season. Gabriel made his case to be one of those quarterbacks, if the situation arises.

articles.title: Drew Allar, Will Howard Struggle in QB3 Battle, Box Score Stats & Highlights from Steelers vs. Bills
articles.summary: Drew Allar and Will Howard were both under center for the Pittsburgh Steelers during the team's 28-27 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Drew Allar and Will Howard were both under center for the Pittsburgh Steelers during the team's 28-27 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.

Howard played the first half of the game before Allar took the field for the second half, although neither player was able to truly stand out.

Here's a closer look at how they performed.

Former NFL QB has theory about Browns' QB pick

The Steelers' first possession of the game with Allar on the field was a successful one, as they opened the third quarter with a 68-yard drive that was capped off by a nine-yard rushing touchdown from running back Eli Heidenreich.

Pittsburgh wasn't able to move the chains as easily afterwards, as the team's next two drives ended with punts.

The Steelers advanced into Bills territory on Allar's fourth drive, but couldn't convert on fourth down with four yards to gain at Buffalo's 41-yard line.

After the Bills took a late one-point lead, Pittsburgh received the ball with an opportunity to move back in front. The Steelers recorded another turnover on downs after a fourth-down pass from Allar fell incomplete, though.

articles.title: Rookie QB Ty Simpson has another efficient game as Rams wrap up preseason
articles.summary: Stetson Bennett IV has apparently won the Rams' QB2 job.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback Ty Simpson might not play much or at all this regular season, but the Rams should feel good about what they saw from him in the preseason.

Simpson, the No. 13 overall pick of this year's NFL Draft, completed a ton of passes Thursday night as he completed what has to be considered a successful preseason. Simpson played a half and completed 18 of 23 passes for 119 yards and a touchdown. It was a similar stat line to his first preseason game, when he completed 21 of 25 passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Despite the good stats in the preseason, it appears Simpson is set for a redshirt rookie season.

Unless there are some injuries or changes to the depth chart, Simpson might not play this season. It appears he will begin his career as the Rams' third-string quarterback behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett IV. Simpson got the start Thursday while the other two rested. That's a strong indication that Bennett has locked up the Rams' backup quarterback job. It's rare for a quarterback drafted as high as Simpson to be on the third team at the beginning of the season, but that's how it appears Simpson's NFL career will start. Though, Simpson's preseason performances at least might give the Rams' staff something to consider when it comes to the No. 2 quarterback job, either heading into the season or shortly into it.

On Thursday night Simpson completed most of his passes, which he has done through the preseason. He has shown he is capable of quick reads and delivering short passes with good timing and accuracy. Simpson completed 12 of his first 13 passes but none of the completions went for more than 10 yards.

Most of Simpson's preseason has been taking what the defense gives him and doing it quickly. The next step in his progression will be taking smart chances downfield when opportunities arise. That's a reason he will be developing while not playing this season. It was still a productive preseason, which ended with Simpson completing 47 of 60 passes (78.3%) for 382 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

There were some missed opportunities at an even bigger night for Simpson and the offense. The Rams got the ball at the Chargers' 14-yard line after a fumble but managed just 5 yards and a field goal. Later the Rams drove to the 1-yard line but were stuffed on consecutive runs on third and fourth down. Those failures are far from being all Simpson's fault, but it would have looked better had those drives ended with touchdowns.

Simpson's best play of the night, and perhaps his best play of the preseason, came on the Rams' first touchdown. Feeling pressure he escaped the pocket to his left. Moving that way, he turned his body while on the move and made a nice throw to Brennan Presley for the score. That play showed a lot of athleticism, which was a reason Simpson was a high pick.

Bennett has been ahead of Simpson all offseason in the race to be Stafford's backup, and Bennett played well enough in the preseason that he hasn't lost any ground. Apparently head coach Sean McVay had seen enough because Bennett sat out Thursday while Simpson played. One of the knocks on Simpson coming out of college was he didn't have much experience. He had 15 starts at Alabama, all of which came last season. Being able to sit and learn is probably good for his development. The Rams hope they don't need any quarterback other than Stafford this season.

Rams fans got a look at Simpson, their presumed quarterback of the future, this preseason. If everything goes right, their next chance to watch him play will come next preseason.

articles.title: NFL Catchup: Simpson Stars, Mendoza Struggles, Seahawks Extend Star & Gabriel Shows Out
articles.summary: Here are the headlines you need to know from Thursday around the NFL.
articles.body: The final week of the NFL preseason is underway, and some quarterbacks are making some strong final impressions before the regular season gets started. Both Los Angeles Rams quarterback Ty Simpson and Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel had standout showings, while Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza didn't have as great a night. Beyond the gridiron, there were multiple deals done on Thursday in the NFC West as the Rams and the Seattle Seahawks prepare for the year ahead. Here are the headlines you need to know from Thursday around the NFL. Simpson Ends Preseason On A High Note After plenty of speculation and criticism surrounding his selection at No. 13 overall, quarterback Ty Simpson continued his strong preseason on Thursday. Simpson led the Rams to three scoring drives against the Los Angeles Chargers, completing 18 of 23 passes for 119 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 yards on the ground. Head coach Sean McVay still hasn’t officially named a backup quarterback behind MVP Matthew Stafford. Stetson Bennett has been in the system for a few years, but with Simpson continuing to impress, he's certainly made a case for himself to be considered for the job. Mendoza’s Preseason Struggles Continue The Las Vegas Raiders played their starters against the San Francisco 49ers, and veteran Kirk Cousins once again looked every bit the part. However, the story was completely different for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. For the second consecutive week, the former Indiana star and Heisman Trophy winner struggled on the field, throwing another interception. Mendoza took over late in the first quarter and played into the third. He completed just 7 of 14 passes for 57 yards and a pick. Head coach Klint Kubiak has been on record all offseason favoring a redshirt year for Mendoza to learn behind Kirk Cousins. So, Thursday's performance might not mean much for Mendoza in the long run. Gabriel Shines Against Patriots The Cleveland Browns named veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson their Week 1 starter earlier this week, with Shedeur Sanders winning the backup job. With the top two spots solidified, former third-round pick Dillon Gabriel had a clear runway to show he's worthy of being Cleveland's third-string quarterback. Gabriel completed 12 of 15 passes for 186 yards and three touchdowns against the New England Patriots on Thursday night. It’s unclear if head coach Todd Monken plans to carry three quarterbacks this season, leaving both Gabriel's roster spot and the future of Arkansas rookie Taylen Green up in the air. If Gabriel wanted to establish himself as a viable option at some point this season, he certainly proved it. If he's not in the long-term plans for the Browns, he might have put enough on film to show the other 31 teams in the league that he’s worth a serious look ahead of final roster cuts. Seahawks Extend Leonard Williams on Three-Year Deal The Seattle Seahawks agreed to a three-year, $90 million contract extension with defensive lineman Leonard Williams on Thursday. The deal carries an average annual value of $30 million, tying Williams with Tampa Bay Buccaneers nose tackle Vita Vea for fifth-highest among interior defensive linemen. Williams was entering the final year of a three-year, $64.5 million contract. The 32-year-old earned second-team All-Pro honors in 2025 after recording seven sacks, 62 combined tackles, and 58 quarterback pressures. Originally selected sixth overall by the New York Jets in the 2015 NFL Draft, Williams was acquired by Seattle from the New York Giants during the 2023 season. The extension follows major offseason deals by Seattle for wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and cornerback Devon Witherspoon. Dolphins Trade Tutu Atwell Back To Rams The Miami Dolphins agreed to trade wide receiver Tutu Atwell back to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for running back Jarquez Hunter on Thursday. The move reunites Atwell with the Rams five months after he departed Los Angeles in free agency to sign a one-year contract with Miami in March. Atwell was originally selected by the Rams in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft and appeared in 64 games over four seasons with the franchise. He rejoins head coach Sean McVay's offense to complement a receiving room featuring Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Hunter, a 2025 fourth-round pick out of Auburn who appeared in five games as a rookie, joins Miami to provide depth in the backfield. The Rams open their regular season against San Francisco on Sept. 10, while Miami opens against Las Vegas on Sept. 13. Latest On Christian Gonzalez, Joey Porter Contract Standoffs The New England Patriots and Pittsburgh Steelers are both navigating contract standoffs with their young star cornerbacks ahead of the regular season, according to ESPN. The Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez remain far apart in negotiations despite early optimism, ESPN reported Thursday. Patriots owner Robert Kraft previously said the team offered a deal to make Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in team history, but Devon Witherspoon’s four-year, $132 million contract extension with Seattle raised the market benchmark. Gonzalez admitted this week that the process has been "frustrating." He has two years remaining on his rookie deal. Meanwhile, the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter do not appear close to a contract extension either, according to ESPN. Porter remains on Pittsburgh's physically unable to perform (PUP) list with a back injury as he enters the final year of his rookie contract. Injury News & Notes

articles.title: Crece el porcentaje de jugadores que murieron por enfermedades cerebrales
articles.standfirst: Así lo apuntan nuevos estudios sobre la encefalopatía traumática crónica (CTE): uno de cada cuatro jugadores que murieron entre 2016 y 2021 sufría esta enfermedad
articles.summary: Así lo apuntan nuevos estudios sobre la encefalopatía traumática crónica (CTE): uno de cada cuatro jugadores que murieron entre 2016 y 2021 sufría esta enfermedad
articles.body: El número de jugadores de la NFL que está falleciendo a causa de la encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC), una enfermedad cerebral degenerativa que sólo puede detectarse después de la muerte, está creciendo, según nuevos estudios. Así, un estudio publicado en la prestigiosa revista 'British Medical Journal' recoge que al menos uno de cada cuatro jugadores que fallecieron en la liga entre 2016 y 2021 padecía esta enfermedad. Daniel Daneshvar, profesor asociado de la Facultad de Medicina de Harvard y autor principal del estudio, apuntó que "nosotros y otros investigadores hemos demostrado que, entre los jugadores de la NFL en particular, la tasa de mortalidad por enfermedades neurodegenerativas es aproximadamente cuatro veces mayor que la de la población general". Durante el periodo estudiado, fallecieron 878 exjugadores, de los cuales 235 donaron sus cerebros para la investigación. Se concluyó que 215 padecían encefalopatía traumática crónica (CTE), lo que significa que al menos el 24,5 % de los jugadores fallecidos durante este periodo padecían CTE. En los últimos años, las familias de exdeportistas de disciplinas como el rugby, el fútbol americano o el hockey hielo que han fallecido deciden donar su cerebro para el estudio de esta enfermedad. Recientemente lo hizo la hija del exjugador de la NHL Claude Lemieux, que murió a los 60 años. De hecho, muchos de estos deportes han introducido cambios en las normativas para proteger a los jugadores tras sufrir una conmoción cerebral durante los encuentros, reglas que incluyen no volver al terreno de juego hasta ser evaluado o los periodos de recuperación que se alargan y que son supervisados por los médicos de forma exhaustiva.

articles.title: Ranking the NFL's 10 Most Clutch Quarterbacks With Games On the Line Entering 2026
articles.summary: "He's clutch!"
articles.body:
You hear the phrase being thrown around constantly, but it's rarely quantified. On the brink of the 2026 NFL season, let's separate narrative from reality by digging into the hard evidence.

By examining advanced play stats from Pro Football Reference dating back to 2020—while factoring in the eye test and high-stakes playoff pedigree—here are the NFL's top 10 most clutch quarterbacks right now.

Unfortunately he wasn't a major factor as a sophomore in 2025, but the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year has still compiled a 109.8 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games early in his career. And that was actually elevated to 117.5 in the 2024 playoffs.

The newly crowned champion has a 110.2 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games in his last two seasons with Minnesota and Seattle. He had some epic late-game performances in victories over the Bears and 49ers in 2024. The overall sample is still pretty limited, though.

The three-time Pro Bowler has a 104.2 third-down passer rating in the second half of one-score games since 2023. And in the fourth quarter of one-score games during that span, he's rushed for 34 first downs (ranking second among all NFL players). The problem? He has a league-high nine interceptions under those circumstances the last three years.

In that same time frame as Hurts, Mayfield has a 115.7 rating on second-half third-down passes in one-score games. Only Lamar Jackson tops that among guys with at least 30 passes. But 2023 (157.9!) is doing most of the work there.

He's just one year in, but the promising 26-year-old posted a 128.6 rating on third-down passes thrown in the second half of one-score games as a rookie in 2025 (ranking third among qualified passers).

This may seem odd considering his broad struggles three years in, but Young has actually led an NFL-high 12 game-winning drives since coming into the league in 2023.

Part of that comes from the fact that the Panthers rarely blow teams out, but his 99.8 third-down passer rating in the second half of one-score games since 2024 indicates a significant clutch factor with the 25-year-old.

Imagine where he could go with more support in key moments in the future.

Purdy posted a ridiculous 132.7 third-down passer rating in the second half of one-score games in 2025, and that mark is 121.0 dating back two full seasons.

He has a 106.5 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score playoff games since 2022, and has led four playoff game-winning drives in his first four seasons in the league.

Particularly memorable were his his calm comeback performances in back-to-back playoff victories over the Packers and Lions in 2023.

The only thing holding Purdy back in this regard is his occasional mistake-prone nature in key late-game regular-season scenarios.

Love has led a tied-for-league-high eight fourth-quarter comebacks since 2023, and he was behind four game-winning drives in 2025.

Like Young, he's backed that up personally with a 116.7 third-down passer rating in the second half of one-score games in 2025 (and 110.6 the last two seasons).

On top of that, per Sharp Football Analysis , Love's 2025 EPA per dropback (+0.31) when trailing in the second half ranked second only to Matthew Stafford.

Two years into his career, Nix has already led 10 game-winning drives (a league-high seven of which came in 2025).

The 2024 first-round pick also posted a 107.3 passer rating in one-score games in the 2025 playoffs, and his EPA per dropback (+0.28) when trailing in the second half ranked third to only Stafford and Love in the regular season.

Nix made his mark converting three critical third downs in a fourth-quarter drive when he nearly toppled the juggernaut Chiefs as a rookie in 2024, and he delivered when needed in an overtime playoff win over the Bills this past January.

Williams flourished while leading a league-high six fourth-quarter comebacks in 2025, bringing his total to an NFC-best eight in two years since entering the league. He led six game-winning drives in the process this season, and posted a phenomenal 130.9 passer rating on third-down throws in the second half of one-score games.

Recently, he orchestrated an unforgettable second-half comeback to help the Bears earn a critical overtime win over the division-rival Packers in a big December matchup.

You get the feeling that's just the tip of the iceberg for the former No. 1 overall pick in Ben Johnson's offense. That said, we need to see more before moving him into the top five.

The 2025 campaign wasn't pleasant for Jackson, but he still managed to post a fantastic 119.1 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games—throwing zero picks on 45 attempts in those scenarios.

In a larger yet more pointed sample, the two-time MVP has 21 passing/rushing touchdowns to just five interceptions on third-down plays in the second half of one-score regular-season games dating back to 2020.

His 108.0 rating under those circumstances in that time frame ranks second among qualified passers, behind only Joe Burrow.

Allen might take some flak for the fact that he hasn't gotten the Bills over the hump in the playoffs this decade, but the reality is he's posted a stellar 116.7 passer rating on third-down passes in the second half of one-score games the last five postseasons.

That's beyond elite considering the competition level in January.

Allen also has a triple-digit rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games the last two regular seasons, and he's generated 33 combined passing and rushing touchdowns to just seven interceptions under those circumstances since 2020.

Highlighting it all is that heroic 2024 win over the Chiefs , but clouding it is the fact he is 0-7 in his career in overtime games despite possessing the ball on six of those occasions.

Speak of the devil. Burrow has a ridiculous 111.6 rating on third-down plays in the second half of one-score games since coming into the league in 2020. That blows Patrick Mahomes, Allen and Purdy out of the water.

That's just one stat, but he also holds his own with a 108.3 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games in the last half-decade.

Although his recent results temper his case somewhat, Burrow remains a proven elite performer in high-pressure situations.

Mahomes is indisputably one of the most clutch playoff performers in league history.

In the last five years, the two-time MVP has a 113.2 passer rating with seven touchdown throws and one interception on 94 passes in the fourth quarter of one-score playoff games.

He's led a tied-for-league-high 17 game-winning drives in the regular season in that time frame, but he's orchestrated six more in the playoffs (as well as five fourth-quarter comebacks, while no other quarterback has more than three during that span).

The reel starts with his late-game heroics in Kansas City's Super Bowl LVIII victory over the 49ers following the 2023 season, but his repeated fourth-quarter successes have made such moments seem routine.

The reigning MVP edges out the legendary Mahomes, mainly because of what he's done for us lately.

Stafford has an eye-popping 115.4 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games since 2024. But if you extend back to 2020, that number only drops slightly to 107.0.

Most recently, in the 2025 playoffs, the 38-year-old led two game-winning drives in the fourth quarter (bringing his total to five in the postseason since 2021) while posting a 109.3 rating with a one-score margin in the final frame of those victories.

Oh, and in terms of that Sharp Football Analysis accounting of EPA per dropback when trailing in the second half in 2025, Stafford crushed his quarterback peers with a mark of +0.45 (Love was the only other qualifier above +0.30, at +0.31).

articles.title: Taylor Rapp, Cedric Tillman Jr., and Early NFL Cuts Who Should Be on Teams' Radar Ahead of Deadline
articles.summary: With the NFL preseason winding down and the 2026 regular season rapidly approaching, teams are scrambling to fine-tune their depth charts.
articles.body:
With the NFL preseason winding down and the 2026 regular season rapidly approaching, teams are scrambling to fine-tune their depth charts.

Teams have until 6 p.m. ET on Sunday to cut their 90-man offseason rosters down to 53 players, and some have gotten an early jump on the deadline.

Unsurprisingly, the list of early cuts—and players who are expected to be cut—includes many NFL hopefuls who will land on practice squads or bide their time as street free agents.

However, some experienced veterans have suddenly become available and ready to help a new team in 2026.

Here, we'll examine the most notable early cuts, what they could provide with a change of scenery, and any relevant recent buzz surrounding them.

On Monday, the Las Vegas Raiders announced that they had released wide receiver Noah Brown. The veteran pass-catcher lasted just over a week with Las Vegas, and he apparently failed to impress enough to stick.

While the 30-year-old didn't mesh with a Raiders team looking to skew young, he could be a strong addition to a contender in need of veteran depth. Brown played just four games with the Washington Commanders last season because of groin and rib injuries. However, the previous season, he caught 35 passes for 453 yards and a touchdown.

In all, Brown has appeared in 91 regular-season games and caught 151 passes for 2,083 yards. He'd make a ton of sense for a playoff hopeful that has employed him before, like Washington or the Houston Texans.

Logical Landing Spots: Houston Texans, Washington Commanders

Offensive lineman Cody Ford has logged snaps at left guard, right guard and offensive tackle since entering the NFL as a 2019 second-round pick of the Buffalo Bills.

He spent the last three years as one of the Cincinnati Bengals' primary backups. While he hasn't been a full-time starter since his rookie season, he has appeared in 99 regular-season games overall.

The Bengals are releasing Ford, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo .

While the Bengals have decided to go in a different direction with their line depth, Ford's experience and positional versatility make the 29-year-old an attractive option for rebuilding teams and contenders alike.

Practically any team in the midst of an offensive-line overhaul should have some level of interest in Ford.

Logical Landing Spots: Cleveland Browns, Houston Texans

After four seasons with the Cleveland Browns, running back Jerome Ford made his way to the Commanders this offseason. However, Washington also added Rachaad White and rookie Kaytron Allen behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, meaning Ford faced an uphill battle to make the roster.

After he suffered a hamstring injury, Ford was waived with an injury settlement, according to ESPN's John Keim .

Naturally, teams will want to know that Ford is healthy before making any contract offers, but the 2022 fifth-round pick should have a lot of value as a depth player. He topped 1,100 scrimmage yards with the Browns in 2023, and he has averaged 4.3 yards per carry over the course of his career. He also won't turn 27 until next month.

If healthy, Ford would be a great insurance policy and change-of-pace back for a potential playoff team with a lack of proven RB depth.

Logical Landing Spots: Dallas Cowboys, San Francisco 49ers

The Commanders signed safety Will Harris to a two-year deal last offseason, but he missed nearly half of the season with a fractured fibula. Washington announced on Tuesday that it had released Harris.

Some teams will undoubtedly be concerned with Harris' age (30), recent injury, and level of play in 2025 ( 117.1 opposing quarterback rating). However, others will be intrigued by his positional versatility and past performances.

Harris has played free safety, strong safety, cornerback, and nickelback. With the New Orleans Saints in 2024, he made 13 starts and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 79.4.

New Orleans is one of two former employers that would make sense for Harris. The other is the Detroit Lions, who are dealing with multiple injuries at safety. Kerby Joseph is battling a knee issue, while Brian Branch is recovering from a torn Achilles. Offseason addition Christian Izien has an undisclosed injury and could miss the start of the regular season.

"I don't know if we will have him for the opener or not," head coach Dan Campbell said of Izien.

Logical Landing Spots: Detroit Lions, New Orleans Saints

Cornerback Nick McCloud signed with the Miami Dolphins on August 10, but he didn't stick with the rebuilding team for long. They announced that they had released the 28-year-old defender on August 22.

A 2021 free agent out of Notre Dame, McCloud has logged starts with the New York Giants, San Francisco 49ers and Chicago Bears. While he's never been a high-end defender—he has allowed an opposing QB rating of 114.9 during his career—he has appeared in 63 games with 20 starts and has also contributed on special teams.

Most teams looking for experienced depth in the secondary and on special teams should at least consider McCloud. However, he might be the most intriguing to a team with schematic familiarity at this point in the offseason. A Bears reunion could make sense, as could a reunion with Colts defensive backs coach Jerome Henderson.

Henderson was New York's DB coach during McCloud's career-best 2023 campaign (17 games, 72.4 opposing QB rating).

Logical Landing Spots: Chicago Bears, Indianapolis Colts

Safety Taylor Rapp started 24 games for the Bills over the past three seasons, but he was limited to only six games in 2025 by a knee injury that required surgery.

The 28-year-old signed with the Denver Broncos on August 20, but they released him less than a week later.

However, there is a chance that Rapp returns to Denver in the near future. Broncos coach Sean Payton told reporters that the safety needed to attend to a personal matter and is a strong candidate to re-sign (h/t Zac Stevens of DNVR).

The Broncos already have a loaded defense. However, they should be interested in bringing back Rapp, who has made 72 starts while allowing an opposing passer rating of 91.0 in his career and who has experience at both strong and free safety. Other teams with questionable safety depth should have an eye on Rapp, too.

Logical Landing Spots: Denver Broncos, Detroit Lions

The Cleveland Browns used two of their first three picks in the 2026 draft on receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston .

With those two in the fold, Cleveland decided it doesn't have room for 2023 third-rounder Cedric Tillman Jr.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Browns will release Tillman.

The Tennessee product recorded just 833 yards in three seasons with the Browns, though it's worth noting he often played in an underwhelming Cleveland offense.

The 26-year-old is still a promising 6'3", 215-pound pass-catcher who did periodically flash for the Browns.

Tillman had 330 yards and three touchdowns in a five-game stretch late in 2024 before suffering a season-ending concussion.

Rebuilding teams with a lack of proven receiver depth should be willing to take a flier on Tillman.

Logical Landing Spots: Las Vegas Raiders, Miami Dolphins

articles.title: Ty Simpson Impresses, Final Box Score Player Stats & Highlights from Rams vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Making his first start in the Los Angeles Rams' preseason finale, Ty Simpson turned in another efficient game to lead a 20-18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Making his first start in the Los Angeles Rams' preseason finale, Ty Simpson turned in another efficient game to lead a 20-18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night.

Simpson played the entire first half and led two scoring drives, including connecting with Brennan Presley for a touchdown early in the second quarter.

Simpson's touchdown pass came out of structure on a blitz from the Chargers that forced him to roll to his left and throw a strike back across his body to Presley.

In three games this preseason, Simpson finished 47-of-60 for 382 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

With the Rams resting all of their regular starters and some key backups, including Stetson Bennett, head coach Sean McVay gave Simpson a lot of runway as he prepares for his rookie season.

Unlike the Rams, Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh used most of his starters for the first two series of the game on both sides of the ball. Simpson was able to get three points out of that, though it comes with a caveat because the Rams recovered a Justin Herbert fumble at the Chargers' 20-yard line.

Four of Simpson's five drives produced at least one first down. His best drive was a 17-play, 79-yard possession to end the first quarter that didn't lead to any points because the Chargers defense stuffed Jordan Waters on fourth-and-goal from the one.

Speaking to Darren Haynes of CBS LA after the win, Simpson expressed happiness with how he has progressed throughout training camp and the preseason while acknowledging there's still a lot of room for growth.

The Rams pulled one of the biggest shockers of the 2026 draft by taking Simpson with the No. 13 overall pick. He is not expected to play this season as long as Matthew Stafford, coming off an MVP in 2025, can remain healthy.

In the event Simpson does get called into action, though, his play in the preseason combined with McVay's scheme and the offensive talent around him suggests the Rams can still play at a high level.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes went from Texas teenagers to one of sports’ most famous couples
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have built a relationship that has grown alongside one of football’s biggest careers. From teenage romance in Tex.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have built a relationship that has grown alongside one of football’s biggest careers. From teenage romance in Texas to a lavish Hawaii wedding and life as parents of three, their story has unfolded in the public eye. Yet, behind the Super Bowl celebrations and glamorous moments, their relationship has been shaped by years of growing up, supporting each other and building a family together.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes: From High School Sweethearts to MarriageLong before Patrick Mahomes became an NFL superstar, Brittany was already part of his life. The two met while attending Whitehouse High School in Texas and began dating as teenagers. Their connection survived the transition from school life to college, professional sports and eventually the intense spotlight that came with Patrick's football career.The couple also attended prom together in 2013, a detail that has become a memorable part of their early love story. Over the years, Brittany has remained one of Patrick's most visible supporters, celebrating major moments in his career while also developing a professional path of her own.Brittany played soccer at the University of Texas at Tyler before pursuing a professional career with UMF Afturelding in Iceland. She later became a certified personal trainer and launched Brittany Lynne Fitness. She also became a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current, connecting her own sporting background with her life in Kansas City.Their relationship entered a new chapter on August 1, 2020, when Patrick proposed at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. The proposal came shortly after the Chiefs received their Super Bowl 54 championship rings and just one day after Brittany's 25th birthday.Brittany later shared her excitement online, writing, "So this happened today!"Patrick showed off her engagement ring on Instagram with the caption "Ring SZN." The couple then celebrated privately with a candlelit dinner.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' Wedding and Growing FamilyMarriage followed nearly two years later. Patrick and Brittany exchanged vows on March 12, 2022, in Maui, Hawaii, surrounded by family and friends. Their daughter Sterling, who had been born in February 2021, also became part of the wedding celebration.The couple welcomed their second child, son Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, on November 28, 2022. His arrival added another chapter to a relationship that had already evolved from teenage dating to marriage and parenthood.Brittany has continued to stand beside Patrick during some of the defining moments of his NFL career. After his Super Bowl LVII victory in 2023, she celebrated on the field with their daughter. The following year, she was again there as Patrick and the Chiefs secured another championship, sharing the celebrations with their children.Their family grew once more on January 12, 2025, when they welcomed daughter Golden Raye Mahomes. With three children now in the family, Patrick and Brittany's journey has moved well beyond their high school sweetheart beginnings.Through every stage, Brittany has remained a familiar presence beside Patrick. Their story is not simply about football victories or celebrity moments. articles.title: Fernando Mendoza-Kirk Cousins QB1 Battle Addressed by Raiders HC Kubiak After Rookie's Struggles
articles.summary: Despite an inconsistent outing by Fernando Mendoza in Thursday's preseason finale against the San Francisco 49ers, Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is still not ready to reveal who their starting quarterback will be in Week 1.
articles.body:
Despite an inconsistent outing by Fernando Mendoza in Thursday's preseason finale against the San Francisco 49ers, Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is still not ready to reveal who their starting quarterback will be in Week 1.

Speaking to reporters after the Raiders' 18-12 loss, Kubiak said the coaching staff will review the tape before making any final decisions between Mendoza and Kirk Cousins.

"I still don't think we need to name anybody," Kubiak said. "We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff."

Cousins started two of the Raiders' three preseason contests, including Thursday night. He didn't play in the Aug. 20 matchup against the Houston Texans.

In his two outings against the 49ers and Arizona Cardinals, Cousins went 13-of-17 for 101 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions and he wasn't sacked. He led the offense to two field goals on his two drives versus the San Francisco defense.

Mendoza went 7-of-14 for 57 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in five drives. The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft finished the preseason 25-of-45 for 240 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions. He was sacked four times.

Kubiak insisted at the start of training camp that Cousins was in line to be their starter. He has been listed as QB1 on the depth chart throughout the entire preseason.

Mendoza's strong preseason debut in which he became the first top overall draft pick to throw a touchdown pass in his first game since Baker Mayfield in 2018 seemed to open the door for a competition.

Cousins starting two of the three preseason games would seem to indicate he remains the frontrunner to start in Week 1, but the Raiders do have to be mindful of Mendoza's development since it is more difficult to get consistent reps in practice during the regular season if you aren't the starter.

Kubiak and his staff still have two weeks before the regular season begins, giving them a window to keep evaluating the situation. The Raiders will host the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium in Week 1 on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Travis Kelce turns childhood nostalgia into a $200 million business move with investment inspired by his Ohio upbringing
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is taking his love for amusement parks into the business world. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has joined investment firm JANA Partners.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is taking his love for amusement parks into the business world. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has joined investment firm JANA Partners in a major stake in Six Flags Entertainment, adding another unexpected name to his growing portfolio. For Kelce, the move has a personal connection too. He grew up in Ohio, where Cedar Point was a familiar part of life, making this investment feel closer to home.Travis Kelce invests in Six Flags with JANA PartnersKelce and JANA Partners announced their investment in Six Flags Entertainment on October 21, 2025. JANA Partners established a 9% stake in the company, valued at roughly $200 million, while Kelce publicly confirmed his involvement through Instagram.His message showed that the deal was not simply about adding another company to his investment portfolio. It connected with a childhood interest that remained close to him.“To all my fellow theme park and amusement park lovers,” Kelce wrote. “I have some exciting news!!! Couldn’t pass up the opportunity to continue the tradition and make Cedar Point and Six Flags even more special for the next generation of families! Excited to partner with JANA Partners as an investor in Six Flags. So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle.”The Cleveland connection helps explain why the deal has attracted attention. Kelce grew up around 65 miles from Cedar Point, one of the best-known amusement parks in the United States.Theme Park Insider editor Robert Niles said the connection made sense because Cedar Point has long been closely associated with Cleveland culture.“I don’t know a single person from Cleveland that doesn’t love Cedar Point,” said Robert Niles, editor of Theme Park Insider. “So, no surprise to me at all that a guy from Cleveland would want to be associated with any effort to make Cedar Point an even better place than it already is.”Six Flags investment comes as company faces major challengesKelce's arrival comes at a difficult moment for Six Flags. The company's stock had fallen more than 45% during 2025, with weather, weaker attendance and growing competition contributing to its struggles.The company also faced pressure following the merger between Six Flags and Cedar Fair. Niles described the situation bluntly.“A lot of people in the industry will acknowledge that Six Flags is a mess right now,” Niles said. “The merger of Six Flags and Cedar Fair has not delivered the benefits that people were hoping for. The headwinds that these parks have been fighting have just been too strong for them. Those two companies had to borrow a lot of money to get through the pandemic, and the shrinking buying power of the middle class has really hurt their core market.”The investment announcement nevertheless created an immediate market reaction. Six Flags shares jumped more than 20% during the session before closing nearly 18% higher.For Kelce, the Six Flags investment also adds another chapter to his expanding business career. Beyond football, he has invested in Formula 1's Alpine team and built commercial partnerships with brands including American Eagle, Subway and State Farm.His growing profile, helped further by his relationship with Taylor Swift, has made him an increasingly recognizable figure beyond the NFL. Now, with Six Flags, Kelce is putting his name behind a business tied to a passion that started much closer to home.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
