articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' Backups Battle with Allar, Howard Addressed by McCarthy Before Steelers' Roster Cuts
articles.summary: Even though there is no drama about who the starting quarterback will be for the Pittsburgh Steelers, the competition behind Aaron Rodgers has been fierce throughout the preseason.
articles.body:
Even though there is no drama about who the starting quarterback will be for the Pittsburgh Steelers, the competition behind Aaron Rodgers has been fierce throughout the preseason.

With the Sunday deadline for teams to cut their rosters down to 53, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy called it a "very accurate evaluation" to assume Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar and Will Howard have all played well enough to earn a spot on the team.

"I feel good about the quarterback room," McCarthy said after Thursday's preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills. "I've been saying it for quite some time, and they've showed it on the field. We got two veterans that we can win with, and we got two young guys that we're excited about the future."

As has been custom for Rodgers in the later stage of his career, he didn't play in the preseason for the Steelers. His absence gave a lot of runway for Allar and Howard to get playing time.

Rudolph at this point in his career is the established veteran backup in Pittsburgh. He is entering his eighth season with the Steelers since being drafted in 2018. His lone year away from Pittsburgh was in 2024 when he signed with the Tennessee Titans.

Not surprisingly, Rudolph looked very efficient in the preseason by completing 10 of 11 attempts for 93 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions.

Allar and Howard are two potential wild cards in the mix given their youth. Howard is entering his second NFL season after being a sixth-round pick in 2025, but he didn't play as a rookie.

The Steelers selected Allar in the third round of the 2026 draft. He was the fourth quarterback off the board after Fernando Mendoza, Ty Simpson and Carson Beck.

Allar received the most reps of the three quarterbacks in preseason, finishing 30-of-54 for 351 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Howard went 26-of-39 for 229 yards and two touchdowns, but his three interceptions is a potential concern.

Coming out of the Steelers' preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, McCarthy said they viewed Allar as a "first-round pick" in this year's draft.

That would seem to indicate Allar is safe to make the roster, but that would also force the coaching staff to potentially make a tough call because few teams carry even three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster.

Cutdown day is at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday for all 32 teams.

articles.title: No Starters, No Problem: Ty Simpson's 2nd-Quarter TD Sparks the Rams' Preseason Sweep
articles.summary: INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — The Los Angeles Rams are ready to get down to the business of living up to their status as the clear early favorite to win the Super Bowl.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — The Los Angeles Rams are ready to get down to the business of living up to their status as the clear early favorite to win the Super Bowl.

They finished off the preseason with a 20-18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night. Two weeks from now, they'll hop on a 16-hour flight to open the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

"And now here we go," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "We know what a great challenge it's going to be."

Ty Simpson threw a go-ahead touchdown in the second quarter and Harrison Mevis kicked two 27-yard field goals for the Rams, who won all three of their preseason games. Simpson finished 18 of 23 for 119 yards.

"I thought he had good command," McVay said. "He's got a great game-day demeanor."

The Rams didn't play any starters in keeping with McVay's approach to games that don't count in the standings. Even backup quarterback Stetson Bennett was held out.

The Rams added a familiar face earlier Thursday, bringing back wide receiver Tutu Atwell while sending running back Jarquez Hunter to the Miami Dolphins. Atwell was drafted by the Rams in 2021. He signed as a free agent with Miami in March but didn't play a regular-season game there.

"He adds depth. It gives us an opportunity to be able to have that speed element, and he can do some different things," McVay said, denying the move had anything to do with a potential league suspension of star wide receiver Puka Nacua.

The Chargers went 1-2 in the preseason, coming off a 41-17 loss to the 49ers last week.

"I liked the response of the entire team from week two to week three of the preseason," coach Jim Harbaugh said. "Many of the things we were working on I saw some real strides. Offensive line would be a big one. Really like the way it's coming together."

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert played just two series. His fumble led to Mevis' first 27-yard field goal early in the first quarter.

Herbert bounced right back, throwing a 65-yard TD pass to Quentin Johnston — the second-longest catch of the receiver's career — on the second play of a drive that lasted 14 seconds and gave the Chargers a 7-3 lead.

"It was double-wow — the route, the throw, the protection," Harbaugh said.

New defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary chest-bumped safety Tony Jefferson after the Chargers forced the Rams to turn the ball over on downs inside the 1-yard line on a drive that lasted 9:41.

Trey Lance took over for Herbert in the second quarter, with his first series ending on a shanked 20-yard punt by JK Scott. The Rams quickly took the lead for good on third-stringer Simpson's 11-yard TD pass to fourth-string receiver Brennan Presley for a 10-7 lead.

Cameron Dicker missed a 49-yard field goal just before halftime, leaving the Chargers trailing 13-7. Known as the most accurate kicker in NFL history, he also whiffed on two extra-point attempts in three preseason games.

Dicker cut the deficit to 13-10 in the third, hitting a 34-yard field goal.

The Rams extended the lead to 20-10 in the fourth on Matthew Caldwell's 8-yard TD pass to Dean Connors.

The Chargers closed to 20-18 on Gregory Desrosiers' 34-yard TD run and third-string quarterback DJ Uiagalelei's 2-point conversion pass to Evan Svoboda.

Rams: QB Caldwell (knee) went out after being hurt on a keeper late in the fourth quarter.

Chargers: WR Dalevon Campbell appeared to hurt his foot in the third quarter.

Rams: Open Sept. 10 against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.

Chargers: Open Sept. 13 against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium.

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, is eyeing a return in the new season even as concerns about his injuries have only grown in the last few days. articles.body: Daejon Labrayae Love allegedly ran a financial fraud scheme beginning in February 2022, using several names, including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love, and Jordan Love, to allegedly cover his tracks.According to court records, Love allegedly duped 26 women across Oregon, California, Washington, and Idaho out of more than $1.3 million by posing as a San Francisco 49ers wide receiver or a wealthy real estate investor on dating apps, including Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, and Facebook Dating, where he met many of his alleged victims.Love was arrested in August 2026, nearly four and a half years after the alleged scheme began. Along with the 35-year-old Love, 18-year-old Taylor Jamie Chan was also arrested for allegedly posing as his financial advisor. When the scheme began, Love would have been 31 and Chan, 14.Daejon Love allegedly gained the women’s trust by promising a future togetherLove allegedly made his victims believe that he wanted to settle down and build a future - and wealth - with them. Using that manipulation, he allegedly gained their trust and convinced them to give him money for fake investments promoted by his supposed financial advisor, Taylor Jamie Chan.He allegedly created fake bank and investment accounts, which he showed to his victims to make the scheme appear legitimate. Love and Chan allegedly staged three-way calls during which they showed victims bogus investment gains and encouraged them to take out personal loans.According to KGW News, Love allegedly created fake Instagram and bank accounts to trick women into believing that he could invest their money and generate massive returns.KGW News shared a video of Love sitting in a car and recording himself saying:“Okay, so I’m on my way to get my mom. I know I get a lot of fans who wanna know how football works or umm… how I got involved in the league...”He then opened the sunroof of his car.Court records state:“DAEJON LABRAYAE LOVE is a 35-year-old male who created fictitious personas to defraud numerous women he met primarily on online dating platforms. Love frequently falsely portrayed himself as a wealthy National Football League player for the San Francisco 49ers or a real estate investor from Switzerland.Love convinced many of his victims that they were in sincere romantic relationships with him and that he was financially savvy and successful to gain their trust. Love advertised nonexistent investments which Love claimed would get massive returns to his victims.”Fake 49ers social media posts allegedly helped sell the NFL personaKGW News further reported that the Instagram account allegedly used by Love showed him wearing 49ers gear and playing catch on the beach. He also reportedly posted Instagram Stories mentioning free agency, “Year 1,” and the Super Bowl - all within the same week.According to the Los Angeles Times, Love and Chan have been charged in federal court in Portland, Oregon, with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.Court documents reportedly include screenshots of fake bank accounts and investment accounts allegedly used as part of the scheme.In one Instagram Story, Love allegedly used Google’s AI Overview - potentially pulling information from fake online accounts created to support his persona - to convince people that he played in the NFL.The AI Overview reportedly read:“Daejon Love is a wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers, and information about his position, contract, and teammate texting habits is available online. He is also associated with the team through various social media content and articles.”Love later attempted to justify the screenshots in another Instagram Story, recording himself while riding his bike and saying:“Okay, those two screenshots posted, that’s Google. articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleepers to Target and Possible Team Names for Your Squad
articles.summary: There's just one preseason game standing between the offseason and the start of the 2026–27 NFL season. And as Labor Day approaches, so too do most fantasy drafts.
articles.body:
There's just one preseason game standing between the offseason and the start of the 2026–27 NFL season. And as Labor Day approaches, so too do most fantasy drafts.

Whether you're a fantasy expert or dipping your toe into the waters, you likely know which players are regarded at the top of their respective positions. But fantasy seasons aren't won on the starters you select in the first three rounds. Injuries happen, bye weeks happen, and suddenly your bench becomes your secret weapon in winning your league.

We'll break down sleeper targets at each of the Flex positions (running back, wide receiver and tight end). These aren't deep sleepers; you'll know many of these names. But they're players who, if deployed correctly, could end up saving your season.

Rankings are courtesy of FantasyPros and use half PPR scoring. FantasyPros defines a sleeper as a player who has "a strong chance to exceed expectations to become surprise difference-makers for fantasy managers."

Have a dream roster in mind but no team name? Borrow one of the following ideas, from player puns to pop-culture references.

articles.title: 49ers' Christian McCaffrey Named to NFL Top 100, Check Out the Updated 2026 Rankings

articles.body:
The NFL Top 100 countdown is entering the final phase after San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey was revealed as No. 6 on the list going into the 2026 season.

McCaffrey moved up 67 spots from last year's ranking after recording 2,126 yards from scrimmage and 17 total touchdowns in 2025.

With just five spots left to be unveiled, here is how the NFL Top 100 stands right now.

6. San Francisco 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey

The reveal of McCaffrey on Friday leaves Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, Bijan Robinson, Myles Garrett and Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the five players still on the board.

McCaffrey had a fascinating 2025 season for the 49ers. His rushing efficiency was close to the worst of his career. He finished with 1,202 yards on the ground, but his 3.9 yards per carry was his second-worst in a season that he played at least 10 games (3.7 in 2017).

Even with some decline in his game as a runner, McCaffrey remains arguably the best pass-catching back in the NFL. The four-time Pro Bowler caught 102 passes for 924 yards and seven touchdowns.

McCaffrey had more receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns than Jaylen Waddle, DK Metcalf and Ladd McConkey.

The 49ers put a lot on McCaffrey's plate with an NFL-high 413 touches during the regular season. He was instrumental in them finishing with 12-5 record despite a roster that decimated by injuries at other positions.

McCaffrey finished fourth in MVP voting in 2025, marking his second top-four finish in the last three years. Saquon Barkley in 2024 is the only other running back with a top-four MVP finish since the Associated Press expanded the vote to a ranked-choice ballot prior to the 2022 season.

articles.title: Schefter's Cheat Sheet for Fantasy Football Sleepers & Value Players Drops amid 2026 Mock Draft SZN
articles.summary: ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter dropped his fantasy football cheat sheet on Friday, highlighting his top value and sleeper picks at each position.
articles.body:
ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter dropped his fantasy football cheat sheet on Friday, highlighting his top value and sleeper picks at each position.

At quarterback, Schefter named Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears and Tyler Shough of the New Orleans Saints as potential mid- and late-round targets.

Williams accounted for a shade under 4,000 passing yards, 30 total touchdowns and just seven interceptions in his first season under head coach Ben Johnson, and he could be poised to take another leap forward in 2026.

As for Shough, he performed much better than expected as a rookie under head coach Kellen Moore, and with first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and running back Travis Etienne joining No. 1 wideout Chris Olave as his top weapons, the pieces are in place for Shough to potentially establish himself as a fantasy starter.

The Jacksonville Jaguars' Bhayshul Tuten is a middle-round running back who Schefter likes. With Etienne now in Jacksonville, veteran free-agent signing Chris Rodriguez is Tuten's only real competition for Jacksonville's starting running back job.

Schefter also mentioned Blake Corum of the Los Angeles Rams as a potential late-round steal. Kyren Williams has been head coach Sean McVay's preferred choice in the backfield the past few seasons, but Corum rushed for 746 yards and six touchdowns, and averaged 5.1 yards per carry last season, so he could force himself into more opportunities.

In a receiving corps with Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter, Parker Washington was the Jags' standout last season, leading the team in receptions (58) and receiving yardage (847). Schefter sees him building upon those totals in 2026.

Schefter chose Ryan Flournoy of the Dallas Cowboys as a deep sleeper at wide receiver as well. Going extremely late or undrafted in most leagues, Flournoy could become a must-start player in fantasy should anything happen to CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens.

At tight end, Schefter went with the Cleveland Browns' Harold Fannin Jr. as one of his top mid-round targets. The Browns' quarterback and offensive situations look to be a mess, but they weren't any better last season when Fannin had 72 catches for 731 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie.

Closing his picks out, Schefter chose the New York Giants' Isaiah Likely as one of his favorite late-round tight ends. Likely will have continuity with John Harbaugh as his head coach, but leaving the Baltimore Ravens means he no longer has to share snaps with Mark Andrews.

Schefter's full collection of value and sleeper picks at quarterback, running back, wide receiver and tight end can be found at ESPN.com .

articles.title: After Surprise Trade, Vrabel Explains Why Kayshon Boutte Was Dealt to Texans Before Patriots' Season
articles.summary: The New England Patriots' surprise decision to trade Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans earlier this week was a product of how much receiver talent the reigning AFC champs added during the offseason.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots' surprise decision to trade Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans earlier this week was a product of how much receiver talent the reigning AFC champs added during the offseason.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained their receiver depth likely meant Boutte would have been a healthy scratch during the regular season if he had remained with the club:

"That was the one place where we do have some depth. I think for all parties involved, that was probably the best thing. Without injuries Kayshon probably would have been inactive, unfortunately. That's just kind of the way it was with him not playing special teams. I tried to thank Kayshon as many times as I could. I texted him again today."

New England sent Boutte to Houston in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick.

The 24-year-old was coming off a promising 2025 season with 551 yards and six touchdowns in 14 games. His 16.7 yards per reception ranked fourth among all players with at least 30 catches.

New England aggressively pursued receiver talent in the offseason, including signing Romeo Doubs as a free agent and trading for A.J. Brown. DeMario Douglas, who was primarily used out of the slot last season, has received significant reps with the first team in camp alongside Brown and Doubs.

Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III all seem likely to make the 53-man roster. Hollins finished third on the team last season in targets (65) and receptions (46).

Williams, who averaged 20.9 yards per catch on just 10 receptions as a rookie in 2025, will fill the role of the downfield threat with Boutte in Houston.

The Texans are probably thrilled to get a receiver with Boutte's ability at this point in the year. They needed a No. 2 receiver after Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in a joint practice with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Tank Dell did return to practice earlier this month, but he seems likely to be brought along slowly since he hasn't played since Week 16 of the 2024 season due to a major knee injury that included a torn ACL, MCL, LCL and meniscus damage.

articles.title: Raiders still not ready to name starting quarterback after final preseason game
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins has put points on the board in all three of his preseason drives.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders' preseason is over. Following an 18-12 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Klint Kubiak and his crew can now focus on Week 1, which is just two weeks away. There's only one problem there … the team still hasn't named a starting quarterback.

Kubiak wasn't willing to make that call following Thursday's game, telling reporters he wanted to watch the tape and then make his decision, per ESPN.

"I still don't think we need to name anybody," Kubiak said after Las Vegas' 18-12 loss at Allegiant Stadium. "We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff."

While Kubiak spent the entire offseason hinting at going with a veteran over No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, the rookie showed some fight in the team's first two preseason games. Those performances had some wondering whether Mendoza was ahead of schedule, and could be named the team's starter for the regular season.

But Week 3 of the preseason threw some cold water on that idea. Mendoza struggled during the contest , while veteran Kirk Cousins led the team on two scoring drives.

Following Thursday's game, Kubiak seemed to hint at his decision, mentioning Mendoza and all the other rookies could use " another three preseason games " to get ready.

With the Raiders' preseason officially over, Cousins has the statistical edge to claim the starting role.

Kubiak wasn't ready to make that call yet, but that didn't bother Cousins, per ESPN.

"Naming something one day could change the next," Cousins said. "You just go about your business each day, methodically, and let the chips fall where they may."

The decision should happen soon. With a little over two weeks left until the regular season, the Raiders need to start looking ahead. Sorting out the team's starting quarterback would go a long way toward accomplishing that goal.

While Mendoza will get his shot eventually, it certainly looks like Cousins — who was always the favorite — wrapped up the job with his performance Thursday. Kubiak will probably agree with that assessment after watching the game tape.

articles.title: Stock up, stock down following the Bills' 28-27 preseason win over the Steelers
articles.summary: Here is the stock report of the Buffalo Bills following Thursday's 28-27 preseason finale win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills (3-0) approached the 2026 NFL preseason with the goal of making sure that the starters were ready to go and that some of the depth options had the chance to show their best stuff. Buffalo's last preseason matchup came on Thursday against the Pittsburgh Steelers (1-2) and while none of the starters played, the Bills were able to come out on top in dramatic fashion.

The Bills beat the Steelers 28-27 on Thursday in their preseason finale thanks to the efforts of players like quarterback Shane Buechele and wide receiver Skyler Bell. Buechele finished the contest having completed 26 of his 38 passes for 196 yards while Bell caught seven of his 10 targets for 49 yards while also taking his lone carry for a 28-yard touchdown.

On the other side, the Steelers are still evaluating quarterbacks Drew Allar and Will Howard to see who will be the backup behind starter Aaron Rodgers and neither one seemed to separate from the other through their play in this game.

With that being said, here is Bills Wire's stock report for the Bills following Thursday's win over Pittsburgh in the preseason finale:

Bell comes into this season as Buffalo's fourth-round pick as the team seeks to bolster the receiving corps as much as possible in an effort to help out quarterback Josh Allen as much as possible. Bell was the featured receiver on Thursday and not only did he step up to the plate, so to speak, but he also showed his ability to make plays with the ball in his hands, whether he caught a pass or ran the football.

As mentioned with Bell, Hardman is one of the receivers that Buffalo brought in as the team seeks to make it further in the playoffs by making sure that there are as many weapons on the field as possible. Hardman's style of play is well known at this point, but one would have hoped that he would have had more of an impact in this game than just one catch for two yards.

As is customary in the preseason finale, the Bills gave players that are fighting for a roster spot some extended run and Jenkins was one of those players that took advantage of the extra time. Jenkins tied for the team lead in total tackles, but all of his six tackles were solo while also picking up a sack and a tackle for loss over the course of his time on the field.

Carter was a third-round pick of the Bills two years ago and with the defensive line undergoing some changes this offseason, he is one of the players that has the chance to earn some playing time in the rotation. However, Carter finished this game with just one tackle so it wouldn't be a surprise to see him having to do what he can in practice to earn more reps on gamedays.

Gore has been trying to make a name for himself in the NFL which is understandably harder for him to do without being compared to his father, but he ended a preseason with one of his best performances. Gore gained just 27 yards and one touchdown on 10 carries, but he did the bulk of his work in the passing game as he caught all five of his targets for 45 yards.

Buechele had a solid outing against a tough Steelers defense, but given that he was the only quarterback that appeared in this game for Buffalo, it was his chance to have a standout performance to potentially shake things up prior to the season opener. However, averaging 5.2 yards per completion along with a 80.6 passer rating will probably keep Buechele as the third quarterback on the roster for now.
